And he an{{ls}}vvering {{ls}}aid, I beleeue that {{sc|Iesvs Christ}} is the {{ls}}onne of God. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=38}}† And he commaunded the chariot to {{ls}}tay: and both vvent dovvne into the vvater, Philip and the Eunuch, and {{sup|‖}} he baptized him. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=39}}† And when they vvere come vp out of the vvater, the Spirit of our Lord tooke avvay Philip, and the eunuch {{ls}}avv him no more. ''14. Sent Peter.''] Some Prote{{ls}}tants v{{ls}}e this place to proue S. Peter not to be head of the Apo{{ls}}tles, becau{{ls}}e he and S. Iohn vvere {{ls}}ent by the Tvvelue, by vvhich rea{{ls}}on they might as vvel conclude that he vvas not equal to the re{{ls}}t. for commonly the Mai{{ls}}ter {{ls}}endeth the man, and the Superior the inferior, vvhen the vvord of Sending is exactly v{{ls}}ed. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=That Peter vvas {{ls}}ent, is no rea{{ls}}on again{{ls}}t his Primacie.}}But it is not alvvaies {{ls}}o taken in the Scriptures, for then could not the Sonne be {{ls}}ent by the Father, nor the Holy Gho{{ls}}t from the Father and the Sonne: nor othervvi{{ls}}e in common v{{ls}}e of the vvorld, {{ls}}eing the inferior or equal may intreate his frend or Superior to doe his bu{{ls}}ines for him, and {{ls}}pecially a body Politike or a Corporation may by election or othervvi{{ls}}e choo{{ls}}e their Head and {{ls}}end him. {{ls}}o may the Citizens {{ls}}end their Maior to the Prince or Parliament, though he be the head of the citie, becau{{ls}}e he may be more fitte to doe their bu{{ls}}ines. al{{ls}}o the Superior or equal may be {{ls}}ent by his ovvne con{{ls}}ent or de{{ls}}ire. La{{ls}}tly, the College of the Apo{{ls}}tles compri{{ls}}ing Peter vvith the re{{ls}}t, (as euery {{ls}}uch Body implieth both the head and the members) vvas greater then Peter their head alone. as the Prince and Parliament is greater then the Prince alone. And {{ls}}o Peter might be {{ls}}ent as by authoritie of the vvhole College, notvvith{{ls}}tanding he vvere the head of the {{ls}}ame.

''17. Did they impo{{ls}}e.''] ''If this Philip had beene an Apo{{ls}}tle'' ({{ls}}aith S. Bede) ''he might haue impo{{ls}}ed his handes, that they might haue receiued the Holy Gho{{ls}}t. but this none can doe {{ls}}auing Bi{{ls}}hops''. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Sacrament of Confirmation, mini{{ls}}tred by Bi{{ls}}hops onely.}}''For though Prie{{ls}}ts may baptize, and anoint the Baptized al{{ls}}o vvith Chri{{ls}}me con{{ls}}ecrated by a Bi{{ls}}hop: yet he can not {{ls}}igne his forehead vvith the {{ls}}ame holy oile, becau{{ls}}e that belongeth only to Bi{{ls}}hops, vvhen they giue the holy Gho{{ls}}t to the Baptized''. So {{ls}}aith he touching the Sacrament of Confirmation in 8 Act. This impo{{ls}}ition therfore of hands together vvith the praiers here {{ls}}pecified (vvhich no doubt vvere the very {{ls}}ame that the Church yet v{{ls}}eth to that purpo{{ls}}e) vvas the mini{{ls}}tration of the Sacrament of Confirmation. Whereof S. Cyprian {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''ep. 73. nu. 3 ad Iubaianum''.}}{{ls}}aith thus, They that in Samaria vvere baptized of Philip, becau{{ls}}e they had lavvful and Eccle{{ls}}ia{{ls}}tical Bapti{{ls}}me, ought not to be baptized any more: but only that vvhich vvanted, vvas done by Peter and Iohn, to vvit, that by praier made for them and impo{{ls}}ition of handes, the Holy Gho{{ls}}t might be povvred vpon them. Vvhich novv al{{ls}}o is done vvith vs, that they vvhich in the Church are baptized, be by the Rulers of the Church offered, and by our praier and impo{{ls}}ition of hand receiue the Holy Gho{{ls}}t, and be {{ls}}igned vvith our Lordes {{ls}}eale.
